contract_grounding.note: Against the assertion as literally written the violation is factual: the 200 result carries none of the four required fields (all MISSING per the declare-first grid check). However, the assertion itself is a mis-distillation of the cited documentation: the actual v1.18.x schema (in-repo generation source docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json) is a oneOf that explicitly documents {"status":"disabled"} as a legal 200 variant and nests raft state as raft_info.role / raft_info.commit — the flat raft_state/commit_index grid exists in no published bundle v0.10.0→v1.18.x, and 'Terminated' is not even a StateRole value in this version's source. So the API violates the contract's text but not the real documentation; the defect signal is an artifact of the doc link, recorded in chain_trace.

source_grounding.verification_rationale: Explicit intent evidence per the v3.4-tightened bar: (a) the response is a deliberately declared tagged enum with doc comments ('Description of enabled cluster', 'Information about current cluster status and structure') whose Disabled arm is dispatched on consensus absence (dispatcher.rs:267); (b) the maintainers' own published API contract at the exact target version — docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json, the generation source of the assertion's cited source_url — explicitly declares {"status":"disabled"} as a documented legal oneOf variant of the 200 ClusterStatus response, and has done so in every published bundle from v0.10.0 through v1.18.x; (c) the contract's asserted grid cannot be found anywhere in the source or any spec history ('raft_state'/'commit_index' as REST field names: zero hits outside internal raft code; 'Terminated': zero hits in lib/*.rs). This is not unannotated silent behavior — the observed payload is the documented, source-declared standalone variant.
